claim: Pune's old city is situated at the confluence of the Mula and Mutha rivers, whose combined stream is known as the Mula-Mutha river.

sources.quote: The old city of Pune is at the confluence of the Mula and Mutha rivers.
However, rising pollution in the Mula-Mutha that flows through the village has led to a fall in the number of birds coming to Kavadi with each passing year.
Khadakwasla is a dam on the Mutha River situated 20 km from the City of Pune. This dam is one of the main sources of water for Pune.

claim: Pune lies on the western margin of the Deccan Plateau, on the leeward side of the Sahyadri mountain range, at around 560 m above sea level.

sources.quote: Pune lies on the western margin of the Deccan Plateau, at an altitude of 560 m (1,840 ft) above sea level. It is on the leeward side of the Sahyadri mountain range, which forms a barrier from the Arabian Sea.
It lies between 18° 32″ North latitude and 73° 51″ East longitude. It lies on the foothills of Sahyadri Mountains.

claim: Pune district is spread triangularly across western Maharashtra at the foothills of the Sahyadri and is divided into the Ghatmatha, Maval and Desh regions.

sources.quote: The landscape of Pune district is distributed triangularly in western Maharashtra at the foothills of the Sahyadri Mountains and is divided into three parts: “Ghatmatha”, “Maval” and “Desh”.
Pune district forms a part of the tropical monsoon land and therefore shows a significant seasonal variation in temperature as well as rainfall conditions.
Pune (Marathi: Puṇē, pronounced [ˈpuɳeː] ⓘ), previously spelled in English as Poona (the official name until 1978), is a city in the state of Maharashtra in the Deccan Plateau in Western India.

claim: The Khadakwasla dam on the Mutha river, about 20 km from the city, is one of the main sources of Pune's water supply.

sources.quote: Khadakwasla is a dam on the Mutha River situated 20 km from the City of Pune. This dam is one of the main sources of water for Pune.
The PMC supplies the city with potable water that is sourced from the Khadakwasla Reservoir.

claim: The Pune Municipal Corporation has sanctioned projects costing over Rs5,500 crore to rejuvenate the Mula-Mutha river and develop its riverfront.

sources.quote: PUNE: The ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) has decided to spend over Rs5,500 crore on the improvement and beautification of the Mula-Mutha river in the coming years.

In 2022, the Pune Municipal Corporation under the ruling party BJP has given its nod to spend over Rs5,500 crore on the improvement and beautification of the Mula-Mutha river in the coming years, in this two mega projects including development of the riverfront (total Rs4,000 crore) and rejuvenation of the river (total Rs1,500 crore) will take place.

claim: Copper plates dated 758 and 768 AD are the earliest references to the Pune region and record Rashtrakuta rule, naming the place Punaka/Punya Vishaya.

sources.quote: Evidence found as copper plates of 758 AD and of 768 AD reveal that the Rashtrakootas ruled this region at that time.
The first reference to Pune region is found in two copper plates dated to 758 and 768 AD, issued by Rashtrakuta ruler Krishna I.
The copper plates of 758 and 768 CE show that the Yadava dynasty had renamed the city as Punakavishaya and Punya Vishaya.

claim: After the Rashtrakutas, the region was ruled by the Yadava dynasty of Devagiri, which held Pune until 1327.

sources.quote: Pune was part of the territory ruled by the Seuna Yadavas of Devagiri from the 9th century to 1327.
Pune was ruled by the Yadava dynasty after the Rashtrakootas.

claim: The name Pune is explained in the Pune Gazetteer as 'Punya', meaning a holy place.

sources.quote: The Pune Gazetteer explains the term Pune as Punya - a holy place.
'Vishaya' means land, while 'Punaka' and 'Punya' mean holy.

claim: The Deccan sultanates ruled the Pune region between 1400 and the early 1600s, after which Mughal rulers held the town until the middle of the seventeenth century.

sources.quote: Mughal rulers then ruled the city till the middle of the seventeenth century.
The Bahamanis, and their successor states, collectively called the Deccan sultanates, ruled Pune region between 1400 and early 1600s.

claim: Aurangzeb temporarily renamed the town Muhiyabad in the early eighteenth century.

sources.quote: Aurangazeb named Pune as Muhiyabad after the death of Shivaji in 1680.

Mughal emperor Aurangzeb renamed a small neighbourhood in central part of the old city as Muhiyabad (the only divergent naming) some time between 1703 and 1705 in memory of his great-grandson Muhi-ul-Milan, who died there.

claim: Lal Mahal, the childhood home of Shivaji, was established in 1630 by Shahaji Bhosale for his wife Jijabai and his son.

sources.quote: The Lal Mahal (Red Palace) of Pune is one of the most famous monuments located in Pune. In the year 1630 AD, Chhatrapati Shivaji's Father Shri Shahaji Bhosale, established the Lal Mahal for his wife Jijabai and son.

The elaborate palace was built in the Pune jagir by the then jagirdar and future mentor of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj, Dadoji Kondadeo in the year 1630 AD with the idea of rejuvenating the recently razed city of Pune.

claim: Shivaji grew up at Lal Mahal with his mother Jijabai, in a palace built by his father Shahaji in the razed city of Pune.

sources.quote: Pune became popular with the rise of Maratha ruler Shivaji. He spent his early childhood in Pune at Lal Mahal, a palace built by his father Shahaji, where Shivaji's mother Jijabai lived for a decade.
Young Shivaji grew up here, and stayed in the Lal Mahal with his mother Jijabai till he captured the Torna fort in 1645.

claim: Tanaji Malusare fell recapturing the Kondhana fort in 1670, after which Shivaji renamed it Sinhagad — the Lion's Fort.

sources.quote: In 1670, Shivaji reconquered the fort for the third time through his Koli Subedar, Tanaji Malusare in Battle of Sinhagad, and the fort came and stayed under Maratha rule till 1689 A.D.

Restoration workers at Sinhagad Fort, 35 km from Pune, have stumbled upon the original commemorative memorial of Tanaji Malusare, the brave Maratha warrior after whom Shivaji is said to have named Sinhagad Fort (Lion's fort). Malusare died in 1670 after being seriously wounded in the Sinhagad battle.
It has a strong historical significance because Maratha warrior Tanhaji fought and died here in the Battle of Sinhagad in 1670.

claim: Sinhagad, formerly Kondhana, is the most prominent fort near Pune, about 25 km from the city on a hill some 1,290 m high.

sources.quote: Sinhagad, ealier known as ‘Kondhana’ is the most prominent and popular fort in Pune.It is located at village Donaje, taluka-Haveli. It is 25 km away from Pune on a hill 1290 m high.

Sinhagad (also known as the Lion's Fort) is an ancient hill fortress located at around 28 kilometres southwest of Pune, India. Previously known as Kondhana, the fort has been the site of many battles, most notably the Battle of Sinhagad in 1670.

claim: Restoration workers at Sinhagad uncovered the original commemorative memorial of Tanaji Malusare, buried under concrete and layers of paint.

sources.quote: The original commemorative memorial of Tanaji Malusare was unearthed by the restoration workers in February 2019.
The stone structure, found buried under cement, concrete, and layers of oil paint, is believed to be around 350 years old.

claim: At Lal Mahal, Shivaji famously cut off the fingers of the Mughal general Shaista Khan as he tried to escape from the window.

sources.quote: Historically, the Lal Mahal is famous for an encounter between Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj and Shaista Khan where Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj cut off the later's fingers when he was trying to escape from the window of the Lal Mahal.

The Lal Mahal is also famous for an encounter between Shivaji and Shaista Khan where Shivaji cut off four fingers of the latter's when he was trying to escape from the first-floor window of the Lal Mahal.

claim: Bajirao I moved the Peshwa's base from Saswad to Pune in 1728, turning a kasbah into a city and making Pune the capital of the Maratha empire.

sources.quote: As the Peshwa, Bajirao moved his base from Saswad to Pune in 1728, marking the beginning of the transformation of what was a kasbah into a city.
Balaji left the Raja in Raghuji's charge and went to Poona, and from this time Poona became the capital of the Maratha empire.
Bajirao moved his administration from Saswad to Pune in 1728, and in the process, laid the foundation for turning what was a kasbah into a large city.

claim: Shaniwar Wada, the fortified palace of the Peshwas, was completed on 22 January 1732 and was the seat of Peshwa power until 1818.

sources.quote: The construction of the Shaniwarwada was completed on January 22, 1732, two years after Peshwa Bajirao began its conception.
Shaniwar Wada is a historical fortification in the city of Pune, India. Built in 1732, it was the seat of the Peshwas of the Maratha Confederacy until 1818.
Constructed by Peshwe Bajirao I in 1732, the wada bears testimony to the rise and fall of the Maratha Empire.

claim: Shaniwar Wada was largely destroyed by a fire in 1828, leaving only the fortification walls and gateways.

sources.quote: On 27 February 1828, a great fire started inside the palace complex. The conflagration raged for seven days.
Most of it was reduced to ashes during a fire in 1828.
The palace was the seat of Peshwa power and later was destroyed by a fire in 1828.

claim: Under Nanasaheb Peshwa, Katraj lake was linked to Shaniwar Wada and the peths by an underground aqueduct that still carries water today.

sources.quote: The water from these storage lakes was brought to a settlement via a long, underground aquaduct stretching 8km across, via a dug channel.
PUNE: An underground duct, which supplied drinking water from Katraj lake to Shaniwarwada and the central Peth areas in the times of the Peshwas, has been discovered here.
Bajirao's son and successor, Nanasaheb constructed a lake at Katraj on the outskirts of the city and an underground aqueduct to bring water from the lake to Shaniwar Wada and the city.

claim: Nanasaheb Peshwa (Balaji Bajirav), the third Peshwa, ruled from 1740 to 1761 and expanded Peshwa administration over Poona.

sources.quote: Nanasaheb Peshwa succeeded Thorala Bajirao Peshwa and ruled the Maratha kingdom from 1740 to 1761.
Balaji Bajirav, alias Nanasaheb, Third Peshwa, 1740-1761.

claim: Nanasaheb Peshwa built the Parvati temple complex on Parvati Hill, long regarded as a pride of Pune.

sources.quote: Nanasaheb Peshwa constructed Parvati Temple complex, which is known to be the pride of the Pune city.
On the southern fringe of the city, Nanasaheb built a palace on the Parvati Hill.

claim: Peshwa rule in Pune ended in 1818, when the British East India Company defeated Peshwa Bajirao II and took over the Peshwa's territories.

sources.quote: The Peshwa rule ended with the defeat of Peshwa Bajirao II by the British East India Company in 1818.
Satara Proclamation, 10th February1818.

claim: The Battle of Khadki (Kirkee) was fought on 5 November 1817 between the British East India Company and the Maratha Confederacy under Appasaheb Bhonsle.

sources.quote: The Battle of Khadki, also known as or the Battle of Ganeshkhind and Battle of Kirkee, took place at modern day Khadki, India, on 5 November 1817 between the forces of the British East India Company and the Maratha Confederacy under the leadership of Appasaheb Bhonsle.
Battle of Kirkee, 5th November 1817.

claim: Pune (Poona) was surrendered to the British on 17 November 1817, after which the East India Company took over Shaniwar Wada.

sources.quote: Poona Surrendered,17th November 1817. During the day Poona was surrendered. The greatest care was taken to protect the peaceable townspeople and order and peace were soon established.
The East India Company took over the Shaniwar Wada, the seat of the Peshwa, on 17 November 1817.

claim: After the 1817 victory the British built a large military cantonment to the east of the city and garrisoned the town of Poona.

sources.quote: It was placed under the administration of the Bombay Presidency and the British built a large military cantonment to the east of the city (now used by the Indian Army).
At Poona city and cantonment were placed details of Artillery and Pioneers, one Regiment of Light Cavalry, one European Regiment, and three battalions of Bombay Native Infantry.
Pune Cantt, also known as Camp, is a military cantonment located in the city of Pune, India. It was established in 1817 for accommodating troops of the Indian Army.

claim: The British took over Shaniwar Wada in 1817 and used the former Peshwa palace to house mentally-ill patients and prisoners.

sources.quote: The British took over the wada in 1817 and used it to house mentally-ill patients and prisoners.
The East India Company took over the Shaniwar Wada, the seat of the Peshwa, on 17 November 1817.

claim: British troops were cantoned at Poona and a brigade was allotted the cantonment at Dapuri, while Pune Camp was established as a military cantonment.

sources.quote: The cantonment allotted for this brigade was at the village of Dapuri about four miles north-west of Poona.
Pune Cantt, also known as Camp, is a military cantonment located in the city of Pune, India. It was established in 1817 for accommodating troops of the Indian Army.

claim: Savitribai Phule Pune University, formerly the University of Poona, was established on 10 February 1949 under the Poona University Act of 1948.

sources.quote: The Savitribai Phule Pune University (formerly known as University of Poona) was established on 10th February 1949 under the Poona University Act, passed by the Bombay Legislature in 1948.
This included the establishment of the University of Pune (now, Savitribai Phule Pune University) in 1949, the National Chemical Laboratory in 1950 and the National Defence Academy in 1955.

claim: The College of Engineering Pune (now COEP Technological University) was chartered in 1854 and is the third oldest engineering college in Asia.

sources.quote: College of Engineering, Pune (CoEP), chartered in 1854 is a nationally respected leader in technical education.
COEP’s precursor, The Poona Engineering Class and Mechanical School was opened in July 1854, with an aim to provide suitable learning to the subordinate officers in the Public Works Department.
The College of Engineering Pune, an autonomous institute of the government of Maharashtra founded in 1854, is the third oldest engineering college in Asia.

claim: Fergusson College was founded in Pune in 1885 by Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Gopal Ganesh Agarkar and other Deccan Education Society founders.

sources.quote: The Deccan Education Societyâs Fergusson College, set up in Pune in 1885 by stalwarts such as Lokmanya Tilak and Gopal Ganesh Agarkar, will be converted into a state university.
It was founded in 1885 by Vaman Shriram Apte, Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Vishnushashtri Chiplunkar, Mahadeo Ballal Namjoshi and Gopal Ganesh Agarkar.

claim: Pune is known as the 'Oxford of the East' because of its concentration of educational institutions.

sources.quote: Pune also has made its mark as the educational epicenter winning itself the sobriquet, 'The Oxford of the East'.
Surrounded with green hills and placid lakes and having a salubrious climate, Pune is known as the Queen of the Deccan and Oxford of the East.
Pune is often referred to as the "Oxford of the East" because of its educational institutions.

claim: Savitribai Phule Pune University is the largest university in India by the total number of colleges affiliated to it.

sources.quote: Pune has over a hundred educational institutes and more than nine deemed universities apart from the Savitribai Phule Pune University (SPPU; formerly University of Pune), which is the largest university in the country based on total number of affiliated colleges.

In 1994-95, the University had 41 post-graduate departments, 209 affiliated colleges and 118 recognized research institutions, with an enrollment of 1,70,000 students for both the under-graduate and post-graduate courses in different faculties.

claim: The formation of MIDC in 1962 drove industrial land acquisition around Pimpri-Chinchwad, and the Bhosari industrial belt dates from the same year.

sources.quote: The formation of MIDC in 1962 resulted in a constant process of industrial land acquisition and the creation of required support infrastructure.
The Bhosari industrial belt came into existence in 1962. There were a handful of industries. The number is now more than 5,000 small, large and big industrial units.
The formation of MIDC in 1962 resulted in a constant process of industrial land acquisition and the creation of required support infrastructure.

claim: Chakan, Talegaon and Pimpri-Chinchwad form the industrial belt of the Pune region.

sources.quote: Hinjawadi is well-connected to the suburbs of Baner and Wakad as well as the industrial areas of Talegaon, Chakan and Pimpri-Chinchwad.
Hinjawadi is in proximity to the suburbs of Baner near Wakad as well as the industrial areas of Talegaon, Chakan, and Pimpri-Chinchwad.
Major industrial areas around Pune are Chakan, Chinchwad, Bhosari, Pirangut, Hinjawadi, Talegaon, Talawade, Urse.

claim: The Pimpri-Chinchwad Municipal Corporation came into existence on 11 October 1982, upgrading a municipal council formed in 1970 from four gram panchayats.

sources.quote: The council existed till 1982 when the state government decided to upgrade it to the status of a municipal corporation. The PCMC, thus, came into existence on October 11, 1982.

On 11 October 1982, the Municipal Council was merged with seven surrounding villages and the PCNTDA area to form the a new Municipal Corporation (Pimpri Chinchwad Municipal Corporation, Pune, and it split apart from the Haveli taluka to become the 15th and newest of Pune district's talukas.

claim: Pimpri-Chinchwad is called the most rapidly developing city in Asia and the third fastest growing city in the country, with a vast network of industrial establishments.

sources.quote: Pimpri-Chinchwad, since its establishment 50 years ago, has grown rapidly. It is often called the most rapidly developing city in Asia. Industry-wise, no other city in Maharashtra has such a vast network of establishments.
In the last two decades, Pimpri Chinchwad is the third fastest growing city in the country.
It is one of the most rapidly developing suburban areas in India and has emerged as the third fastest growing city in the country.

claim: Automobile majors including Bajaj Auto and Tata Motors have manufacturing plants in Chakan near Pune.

sources.quote: The city is known for its automotive industry. A large number of automobile companies such as Bajaj Auto, Tata Motors, Mahindra & Mahindra, Skoda cars, Mercedes Benz, Force Motors, Kinetic Motors, General Motors, Land Rover, Jaguar, Renault, Volkswagen, and Fiat have there manufacturing plants in Chakan.
Hinjawadi is well-connected to the suburbs of Baner and Wakad as well as the industrial areas of Talegaon, Chakan and Pimpri-Chinchwad.
Hinjawadi is in proximity to the suburbs of Baner near Wakad as well as the industrial areas of Talegaon, Chakan, and Pimpri-Chinchwad.

claim: Bajaj Auto, the Pune-headquartered two- and three-wheeler manufacturer, runs science-and-technology skill development programmes for youth.

sources.quote: Bajaj Auto, headquartered in Pune, is ranked as the world's fourth largest two and three wheeler manufacturer.
Bajaj Auto is committed to promoting science and technology as part of its CSR focus areas i.e. Skill-development in STEM.

claim: The Rajiv Gandhi Infotech Park at Hinjawadi spreads over about 2,800 acres and houses offices of over 800 companies.

sources.quote: It houses the Rajiv Gandhi Infotech Park, a large tech and business park spread over 2,800 acres, which was built by the Maharashtra Industrial Development Corporation. The business park has offices of over 800 companies.

After Bengaluru, the reverberations of downsizing are being felt acutely across the 2,800-acre Hinjewadi IT Park, which houses all the big guns: Infosys, Wipro, Cognizant, IBM and Tech Mahindra, among others.

claim: Hinjawadi's IT parks hold over 165 offices of top corporates employing about 1.5 lakh people.

sources.quote: The development of the Rajiv Gandhi Infotech Park has transformed Hinjawadi from a suburb to a booming commercial district. Also known as the Hinjawadi Park, it occupies 2800 acres and has over 165 offices of top corporates. These offices collectively employ about 1.5 lakh people.
The RGIP, also known as Hinjawadi IT Park, occupies 2,800 acres and has over 165 offices of top corporates. As many as 1.5 lakh people are employed in Hinjawadi alone.

claim: The Rajiv Gandhi Infotech Park at Hinjawadi was built by the Maharashtra Industrial Development Corporation at a cost of Rs 155 crore.

sources.quote: Built at a cost of Rs 155 crore by MIDC, the IT park is challenged by chaotic traffic, insufficient security arrangements and shortage of power supply among many other things.
It houses the Rajiv Gandhi Infotech Park, a large tech and business park spread over 2,800 acres, which was built by the Maharashtra Industrial Development Corporation.

claim: Pune's Hinjawadi IT park alone houses more than 800 companies, and the city has further IT parks at Magarpatta and Kharadi.

sources.quote: Besides Hinjewadi, Pune is home to more than 800 IT companies of all sizes, besides having two other IT parks at Magarpatta and Kharadi.
The IT Park encompasses an area of about 2,800 acres (11 km2) and is home to over 800 IT companies.
The business park has offices of over 800 companies.

claim: Pune's IT sector is a major source of employment, with hundreds of thousands of people depending on it for their livelihood.

sources.quote: As of 2017, the IT sector employed more than 300,000 people.
Over three lakh people in the city depend on the IT sector for their livelihood.

claim: Hinjawadi is popularly known as Pune's Silicon Valley and is the anchor of the western Indian IT industry.

sources.quote: Popularly known as Pune’s Silicon Valley, Hinjawadi has the presence of top multinationals.
It has made this region the Silicon Valley of western India.
Hinjawadi (also incorrectly spelt Hinjewadi and Henjewadi) is a suburb in Pune, India.

claim: Ganeshotsav is Pune's premier festival, with the Dagadusheth Ganapati among the city's most honoured Ganpatis, a public form given to the festival by Bal Gangadhar Tilak.

sources.quote: Years later, when Lokmanya Tilak started the practice of organising annual Ganesh Chaturthi celebrations in Maharashtra, Dagdusheth Ganpati gained fame as the most adored deity in Pune.

Ganesh Chaturthi is widely and publicly celebrated in Pune. Lokamanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak started the public celebration of the festival as a means to circumvent the colonial British government ban on Hindu gatherings through its anti-public assembly legislation in 1892.

It is the most popular among the thousands of deities that are housed in the lanes and bylanes of Pune city, including the big five Ganpatis that are considered of high honour during the annual festival.

claim: The Dagadusheth Halwai Ganapati temple, in Pune's Budhwar Peth, was founded after the halwai couple lost their son in a plague epidemic and is visited by over a hundred thousand devotees a year.

sources.quote: The story dates back to more than 125 years when Shri Dagdusheth Halwai and his wife Lakshmibai lived in Pune. As fate would have it, they lost their only son to the plague epidemic.
The temple is visited by over one hundred thousand devotees every year.
The Dagadusheth Halwai Ganapati holds the rare distinction of being named after a devotee, its inceptor; but it wasn’t always called so.

claim: The monsoon reaches Pune in June, with the heaviest rainfall in July and August, and most of the district's rain falls during the monsoon months.

sources.quote: Most of this rain is brought by the southwest monsoon winds during the summer and about 87% of rainfalls during the monsoon months. The monsoon arrives in the month of June, with the maximum intensity of rainfall during the month of July and August.
Most of the 822 mm (32.36 in) of annual rainfall in the city falls between June and September, and July is the wettest month of the year.
September to June is the best time to visit Pune. The winters are fairly cool and the monsoons have heavy rains.

claim: Ganeshotsav is the most important and biggest festival of Pune, falling in the bright fortnight of Bhadrapada, with public pandals holding idols for five to ten days.

sources.quote: This is the most important and biggest festival in Pune. It falls on the 4th day of the bright fortnight of Bhadrapada (August - September). People buy Ganesh images to keep in their houses as a divine guest for five to ten days.
Ganesh Chaturthi is widely and publicly celebrated in Pune.

claim: Pune is the cultural capital of Maharashtra, a centre for Marathi theatre, music, literature and education.

sources.quote: Pune, the cultural capital of Maharashtra, is an important city of India.
The city leads as the 'veritable heartland' of cultural Maharashtra.

Pune has historically been a major cultural centre, with important figures like Dnyaneshwar, Shivaji, Tukaram, Baji Rao I, Balaji Baji Rao, Madhavrao I, Nana Fadnavis, Mahadev Govind Ranade, Gopal Krishna Gokhale, Mahatma Jyotirao Phule, Savitribai Phule, Gopal Ganesh Agarkar, Tarabai Shinde, Dhondo Keshav Karve, and Pandita Ramabai doing their life's work in Pune City or in an area that falls in Pune Metropolitan Region.
